Spur and high-colour apple strains: Scarlet Spur-II, Red Chief, Super Chief, Oregon Spur, Jeromine

By Gafar Laiya, Gujarat Bio Organics · Updated 2026-11-25

Modern Indian high-density blocks plant high-colour Delicious strains: compact spur types (Scarlet Spur-II, Red Chief, Super Chief), semi-spur Oregon Spur and King Roat, and standard-vigour high-colour strains such as Jeromine, Red Velox and Red Cap Valtod. They colour earlier than old Royal Delicious, especially at 4,500–6,000 ft.

Spur & high-colour strains
Tree habit and fruitCompact spur (Scarlet Spur-II, Red Chief, Super Chief); semi-spur (Oregon Spur, King Roat); standard vigour high-colour (Jeromine, Red Velox, Red Cap Valtod)
Chilling needSpur types 1,000–1,200 hours (4,500–7,500 ft); Oregon Spur 900–1,200; Jeromine and Red Velox 900–1,200 hours (4,500–8,000 ft)
Role in the orchardMain varieties; all need 25–33% pollinizers
StrengthsDark red colour earlier, even at 4,500–6,000 ft; high pack-out of coloured fruit at lower belts (Jeromine, Red Velox).
WeaknessesSpur types give small fruit on M.9 in poor soil; Jeromine and Red Velox turn too dark above about 7,500 ft.

Choose by altitude and soil. Spur strains suit medium-density blocks on MM.106 or MM.111; on M.9 they need deep, fertile, irrigated soil or the fruit stays small. Jeromine and Red Velox give a high share of coloured fruit in lower belts but can colour too dark above 7,500 ft (Himachal package of practices).

Rootstock, spacing and feeding

Choose the rootstock by soil, not by variety alone: M.9 only on deep, fertile, irrigated land with a trellis; MM.106 only on well-drained soil; MM.111 on drier slopes (rootstock guide). Feed by tree age with our apple fertilizer calculator.

Pollination

Keep 25–33% compatible pollinizers flowering at the same time, 4–6 beehives per hectare at bloom, a boron spray at pink bud, and no sprays during full bloom.

Compare: all apple varieties and rootstocks.

Questions farmers ask

How much chilling does Spur & high-colour strains need?

Spur types 1,000–1,200 hours (4,500–7,500 ft); Oregon Spur 900–1,200; Jeromine and Red Velox 900–1,200 hours (4,500–8,000 ft).

Does Spur & high-colour strains need a pollinizer?

Main varieties; all need 25–33% pollinizers.

What are the problems with Spur & high-colour strains?

Spur types give small fruit on M.9 in poor soil; Jeromine and Red Velox turn too dark above about 7,500 ft.
